newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Franc fort challenged, dollar/shares dull.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Franc fort challenged, dollar/shares dull.

text.p: The French franc remained on the sick list on Thursday after overnight pressure on the currency prompted the Bank of France to intervene on its behalf.
Otherwise Europe's key financial markets were quiet in morning trading with the dollar confined to narrow ranges, while European shares were mostly firmer.
The mark spiked up to 3.4315 francs overnight, its strongest level since March 22, and dealers said the French central bank intervened to buy francs at 3.4300 in early European business.

A larger-than-expected increase in German second-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) dealt an extra blow to the franc after Wednesday's data showing the French economy shrank more than had been expected in the second quarter.

"This has been triggered by the GDP report from Germany which has been a lot stronger than forecast and contrasts quite sharply with what's going on in France," said Michael Lewis, senior international economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
By midday, the franc was at 3.4280 per mark, having struggled back to Wednesday's late European level. Its old Exchange Rate Mechanism floor was 3.4305 per mark.
"The BoF is doing a smoothing operation rather than trying to reverse the trend. It's all being done through French banks and volume doesn't appear to be large," said one trader.
Analysts said the market would keep hammering at the franc at least until the 1997 budget was officially presented on September 18. Key details of the budget plans are already known.
German second-quarter GDP rose 1.5 percent on the quarter, compared to consensus forecasts of 1.1 percent and a first-quarter fall of 0.5 percent.
That compares with France's 0.4 percent quarter-on-quarter GDP drop, down from a 1.1 percent rise in the first quarter.

The Bank of France monetary policy council meets during the morning with the results not forecast to reveal any change in policy. Germany's Bundesbank council also met but left rates unchanged, as the markets had expected.
Meanwhile, the dollar continued to hold its narrow range and at midday was quoted at 1.4815 marks and 109 yen, little changed from its late European levels on Wednesday.

European share prices were were mostly firmer on the back of Wall Street's 8.51 point gain on Wednesday. But fears over Friday's U.S. jobs report -- seen as a significant indicator of the trend in the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy -- kept a cap on trade and prices.
"I think we will see rates going up in the U.S. and short-term the market is looking very tricky," said one British based trader.

In London, FTSE-100 Index stood some 13 points firmer at midday after British rates were unchanged at the morning's money market operations, steadying nerves about a possible politically- motivated rate cut.
French stocks extended their opening gains as investors were encouraged by a rash of good corporate results -- notably from Danone and Carrefour.
Traders said the market was waiting for Prime Minister Alain Juppe's tax reform address this evening.
German shares were down a touch by midday after opening steady. The market shrugged off a small rise in German jobless data for August but buying was limited.
CURRENCIES AT 1100 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4815 marks and 109 yen after 1.4815 marks and 108.80 yen late on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1100 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 13.1 points at 3,885.8.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index was down 1.68 at 2,530.71.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 11.59 at 1,996.36.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $386 an ounce, compared with $385.65 late on Wednesday.
